types.name: BeamSplitterElementInput
types.description: The fields a BEAM_SPLITTER element reads. Published for codegen; the wire type is the flat OpticalElementInput

types.name: BeamState
types.description: Beam properties carried on a light edge

types.name: BeamStateInput
types.description: State of the optical beam on a particular path segment.

types.name: BigFileAccessGrant
types.description: Temporary S3 credentials for reading a big file.

types.name: BigFileStore
types.description: A BigFileStore represents a large object stored behind the S3 datalayer.

fields.name: accessGrant
fields.description: Get temporary S3 read credentials for the object.

fields.name: maxBytes
fields.description: The byte budget the upload grant advertised for this store. Advertised, not enforced: a session policy bounds what a credential may write, never how much, so a store may exceed this

fields.name: sizeBytes
fields.description: How many bytes this store actually holds, measured when its upload was finished. Null while unfinished, or for stores written before this was recorded

types.name: BigFileUploadGrant
types.description: Temporary S3 credentials for uploading a big file.

types.name: BlendNode
types.description: Composites its children using an in-layer blend mode

fields.name: label
fields.description: An optional human-readable label for the node

types.name: Blending
types.description: The blending mode used to combine multiple channels or layers into a composite image.

enumValues.name: ADDITIVE
enumValues.description: Additive blending, where the color values of overlapping layers are summed.

enumValues.name: MULTIPLICATIVE
enumValues.description: Multiplicative blending, where the color values of overlapping layers are multiplied.

enumValues.name: NORMAL
enumValues.description: Alpha-over compositing: the layer is blended over the layers below using its opacity.

types.name: Boolean
types.description: The `Boolean` scalar type represents `true` or `false`.

types.name: BootstrapLayerKind
types.description: The render recipe an image layer carries: which default graph createSceneFromCoordinateSystem builds, via `ScenePolicyInput.kind`.

enumValues.name: INTENSITY
enumValues.description: One additively-blended INTENSITY layer per channel, each with its own colormap, order and visibility (a single grey layer when there is one channel). The fluorescence default, and the fallback when nothing else is inferred.

enumValues.name: LABEL
enumValues.description: A single categorical source mapping discrete integer labels to distinct colors. Never inferred from structure -- nothing about an array distinguishes a label map from an image -- so it comes either from a derivation declared CATEGORIZED or from stating it outright.

enumValues.name: RGB
enumValues.description: Composite three channels as red, green and blue in a single layer -- a photograph, a brightfield slide. Never inferred from *shape*: a flat three-channel image is a three-marker fluorescence acquisition far more often than a photograph, and the two cannot be told apart that way. It is inferred from what ingest recorded -- three channels labelled red, green and blue (whose order then decides the components), or a source file that is a PNG or a JPEG -- so pass it for a photograph nothing recorded. Every other recipe gives each channel a layer of its own; this one keeps them together, because red, green and blue are components of one picture.

enumValues.name: VECTOR
enumValues.description: A single VECTOR layer drawing the dataset's vectors as glyphs. Inferred whenever the dataset carries a DISPLACEMENT value axis -- like LABEL's CATEGORIZED edge, that axis type is something an author stated rather than a shape to guess from, so the inference is reading a declaration back. There are no channels to peel: the value axis's positions are components of one offset, not signals to layer separately.

enumValues.name: VOLUME
enumValues.description: One INTENSITY layer per channel as above, each with `projectionMode` set to MIP. Inferred when the dataset has a z axis with more than one plane. The one member with no `LayerKind` of its own: a projection is a setting on one channel, not a kind of layer.

types.name: BoundingBox
types.description: An axis-aligned bounding box, as a min and a max corner

fields.name: max
fields.description: The upper corner, in the coordinate order of the coordinate system

fields.name: min
fields.description: The lower corner, in the coordinate order of the coordinate system

types.name: BoundingBoxInput
types.description: An axis-aligned box as a min and a max corner, in the coordinate order of the frame it is asked in

types.name: ByDimensionTransformInput
types.description: The fields a BY_DIMENSION member of TransformInput reads. Published for codegen; the wire type is the flat TransformInput

types.name: ByDimensionTransformation
types.description: A composition of child transformations, each acting on a named subset of the axes

fields.name: input
fields.description: The system this edge maps from. Null for the child of a SEQUENCE or BY_DIMENSION, which takes its endpoints from the wrapper

fields.name: inputAxes
fields.description: The names of the input axes this edge's parameters are ordered by. `scale`, `translation` and the columns of `affine` follow this order -- which is the input system's axis order, NOT the reading layer's axis names, and the two differ often enough that indexing the arrays against them silently misplaces them. A BY_DIMENSION edge names only the subset of axes it acts on; the axes it does not name are the ones it leaves untouched

fields.name: invariance
fields.description: Which geometric properties survive this edge's map, derived from `kind`: ISOMETRY (distances, angles and areas all transfer), SIMILARITY (angles and length ratios transfer, absolute lengths scale by one common factor), AFFINE (parallelism and area ratios transfer, angles and distances do not), DIFFEOMORPHIC (topology at best, and only locally -- the Jacobian varies with position), NONE (nothing corresponds). A SEQUENCE or BY_DIMENSION is the weakest of its children. Stated by kind, never by inspecting the numbers: an AFFINE edge reads AFFINE even when its matrix happens to be rigid, because separating those needs an SVD. A layer's `placementInvariance` is the minimum of this over its whole path to world

fields.name: output
fields.description: The system this edge maps to. Null for the child of a SEQUENCE or BY_DIMENSION, which takes its endpoints from the wrapper

fields.name: outputAxes
fields.description: The names of the output axes this edge produces. For a rank-changing BY_DIMENSION edge (placing a (c,y,x) dataset into a (t,z,y,x) world) this is the subset it maps onto; the world's other axes are untouched

fields.name: provenanceEntries
fields.description: Provenance entries for this edge: who authored it, and every refinement since. A refinement rewrites the edge in place, so this audit trail is where the placement's earlier states live -- and counting these rows along a chain is what `CoordinateSystem.transformVersion` reports

fields.name: selector
fields.description: Where along one axis this edge applies, or null for an edge that holds everywhere -- which is almost every edge. A per-channel correction is scoped to {axis: "c", index: 2}; several such edges over one axis are one piecewise map. A path query crosses a scoped edge only when it fixes that coordinate with `at`

fields.name: transformations
fields.description: The child transformations. Each carries the `inputAxes` and `outputAxes` it acts on

fields.name: validity
fields.description: How much this map is actually known: VALIDATED for a map the server derived (or one someone checked), INFERRED for numbers read from metadata, MANUAL for an authored registration, UNKNOWN for one its author marked as a guess. A layer's validity is the weakest edge on its path to world

fields.name: valueRelation
fields.description: (derivation edges) What the operation this edge records did to the *values*, orthogonal to `kind`: IDENTICAL (a crop -- statistics transfer), TRANSFORMED (a deconvolution -- same quantity, new numbers), CATEGORIZED (a threshold -- values became labels, and a bootstrapped scene renders the data as a label map). Null when unstated, and never present on a registration -- values do not cross a claim between spaces

fields.name: version
fields.description: How many times this edge has been written, counting the row that created it -- so a new edge reads 1. Only comparison is meaningful: this and the edge's `id` together are the cache key for anything derived from the edge, and a change means refetch. It counts the same provenance rows `provenanceEntries` lists, so the audit trail and the token cannot disagree; a rename moves it too, which errs towards refetching something that did not change rather than trusting something that did

types.name: ByteCount
types.description: A number of bytes. 64-bit, unlike Int: serialized as a JSON number, and accepted as a number or a numeric string.

types.name: CCDElement
types.description: Detector

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Element kind

fields.name: label
fields.description: Element label

fields.name: ports
fields.description: List of ports on the element

fields.name: pose
fields.description: 3D pose of the element

types.name: CCDElementInput
types.description: The fields a CCD element reads. Published for codegen; the wire type is the flat OpticalElementInput

types.name: CameraState
types.description: Where a viewer's camera is in a scene, and how it is looking at it. Carries a flat cross-section view and a volumetric projection view of one position, so a single pose serves both and `Scene.preferredView` picks which is used. Every number is read against the scene's world coordinate system, whose axes carry the units

fields.name: crossSectionOrientation
fields.description: The flat view's orientation, as a quaternion. Null to leave it to the viewer.

fields.name: crossSectionScale
fields.description: The flat view's zoom, in world units per screen pixel. Null to leave it to the viewer.

fields.name: position
fields.description: Where the camera is centred, keyed by the world's axis names. Keyed rather than a positional list because the world's axes are named and a tour through a timelapse moves in t as much as in z -- a list would silently depend on axis order. Axes the pose does not name are left wherever the viewer already had them.

fields.name: projectionOrientation
fields.description: The volumetric view's orientation, as a quaternion. Null to leave it to the viewer.

fields.name: projectionScale
fields.description: The volumetric view's zoom, in world units per screen pixel. Null to leave it to the viewer.

types.name: CameraStateInput
types.description: Where a viewer's camera is in a scene, and how it is looking at it. Give the flat view, the volumetric view, or both -- one pose serves either, and `Scene.preferredView` picks which a viewer opens. Every number is read against the scene's world coordinate system, whose axes carry the units, so they are bare numbers here

inputFields.name: crossSectionOrientation
inputFields.description: The flat view's orientation, as a quaternion. Null to leave it to the viewer.

inputFields.name: crossSectionScale
inputFields.description: The flat view's zoom, in world units per screen pixel. Null to leave it to the viewer.

inputFields.name: position
inputFields.description: Where the camera is centred, keyed by the world's axis names. Keyed rather than a positional list because the world's axes are named and a tour through a timelapse moves in t as much as in z -- a list would silently depend on axis order. Axes the pose does not name are left wherever the viewer already had them.

inputFields.name: projectionOrientation
inputFields.description: The volumetric view's orientation, as a quaternion. Null to leave it to the viewer.

inputFields.name: projectionScale
inputFields.description: The volumetric view's zoom, in world units per screen pixel. Null to leave it to the viewer.

types.name: ChangeFolderInput
types.description: Input for changing an existing folder's name or parent

inputFields.name: id
inputFields.description: The ID of the folder to change

inputFields.name: name
inputFields.description: The name of the folder

inputFields.name: parent
inputFields.description: The ID of the parent folder to nest this folder under

types.name: ChannelLabel
types.description: The channel truth: a human-readable label for a channel, pinned to a coordinate anchor

types.name: ChannelSourceNode
types.description: A single intensity channel of the layer's lens, with its own transfer function

fields.name: label
fields.description: An optional human-readable label for the node

types.name: Chart
types.description: A composition of data laid out along one metric axis, with values read off it. The second kind of composition beside a scene: a scene is a place, a chart is an axis. It names data by id and owns none of it, and it carries no unit of its own -- the unit is its world axis's

fields.name: axis
fields.description: The one axis this chart is laid out along: its name, its metric type and its unit. The world's only axis, repeated here so a client drawing the chart need not unwrap a list of one

fields.name: descriptors
fields.description: This object's descriptors, a flat mapping of key to value: the facts about it that an action's port can `require` and a trigger can test (e.g. `@mikro/n_channels`). The keys are the ones mikro declares for this structure, and the values are the ones a signal about the object carries. Empty for a structure that declares none

fields.name: layers
fields.description: The layers drawn in this chart, back to front (a heterogeneous list of layer kinds)

fields.name: worldCoordinateSystem
fields.description: The space this chart is laid out along. Never owned by the chart: several charts can share it, it outlives each of them, and deleting a chart never deletes it. Ask it for `placedSystems` to learn what could be drawn here

inputFields.name: coordinateSystem
inputFields.description: Filter to the charts laid out over this coordinate system

inputFields.name: ids
inputFields.description: Filter by list of IDs

inputFields.name: search
inputFields.description: Search by name (case-insensitive substring)

types.name: ChartLayer
types.description: A layer drawn in a chart. It carries view state only. Where its data sits along the chart's axis -- `pathToWorld`, `asAffine`, `alongAxis`, `placement`, `placementValidity`, `placementInvariance` -- is derived from the graph on read and stored nowhere, so refining one registration moves every layer that looks through it. The concrete kind says what the layer reads: TraceChartLayer an array, SeriesChartLayer a table, AnnotationChartLayer drawn marks

fields.name: alongAxis
fields.description: The name of the source axis that runs along the chart's axis: for a trace, the axis of its lens the values are read along; for a series, the table's coordinate column; for an annotation layer, the axis of the drawing space that is the chart's own. **Not a setting.** It is the one source axis the composed placement reads the chart's axis from, so it follows the registration: re-register the data by another axis and this changes with no write to the layer. Null when the layer is no longer placed, or is placed by a map that reads the chart's axis from several source axes

fields.name: asAffine
fields.description: This layer's whole `pathToWorld` composed into one affine map: a single row, because the chart's world has a single axis. The coefficient on `alongAxis` is the scale from a step along the data to a step along the chart's axis, in the axis's unit, and the last entry is the offset. Derived on read. Null when `pathToWorld` is null; an error when a path exists but does not condense

fields.name: color
fields.description: The colour the layer is drawn in, as RGBA. Null lets the viewer choose

fields.name: pathToWorld
fields.description: The path of transformation edges from this layer's source coordinate system to its chart's world. Null when the layer is unregistered; empty when the source already is the world. `asAffine` is the same path composed

fields.name: placement
fields.description: Whether this layer has a place along its chart's axis, and if not, why not. UNREGISTERED is a gap to close; UNMAPPABLE is a fact to badge; CONDITIONAL is a placement to ask again for with `at`. Derived, never stored

fields.name: placementInvariance
fields.description: Which geometric properties survive the walk from this layer's data to the chart's world: the weakest edge on its path. Derived, never stored

fields.name: placementValidity
fields.description: How much this layer's placement is actually known: the weakest edge on its path to the chart's world. Derived, never stored

inputFields.name: chart
inputFields.description: Filter by the chart this layer is drawn in

inputFields.name: ids
inputFields.description: Filter by list of IDs

types.name: ChartLayerKind
types.description: The kind of a chart layer, which says what it reads -- never how it looks. TRACE reads an array along one axis; SERIES reads one column of a table against another; ANNOTATION reads drawn marks. A line, markers, both or steps is `ChartMark`, a setting on the layer.

types.name: ChartMark
types.description: How a trace or a series is drawn. A look, not a kind: changing it changes nothing about what the layer reads.

types.name: ChartPolicyInput
types.description: How a chart is drawn from what is already placed in a space

types.name: ClearCoordinateSystemInput
types.description: Input for clearing a shared coordinate system: delete every registration INTO it in one call, keeping the space, its scenes, and its own claims into wider spaces

inputFields.name: id
inputFields.description: The ID of the shared coordinate system to clear

types.name: ClearSceneInput
types.description: Input for clearing a scene: delete every layer, keep the scene and everything it composes over

inputFields.name: id
inputFields.description: The ID of the scene to clear

types.name: Client
types.description: An OAuth client (application) that can act against the API, e.g. the app a change was made through.

types.name: ColorByOption
types.description: One column a layer may be coloured or filtered by, and how it is reached. Both pickers read the same options: `colorBys` and `filterBys` turn on the same measure-vs-categorical split, so two lists would be two copies of one answer. Every option returned is one the mutation that publishes the picker accepts -- `createMeshLayer` over a collection, `createLabelLayer` over a lens -- and every column it omits is one that mutation refuses; that invariant is why this exists rather than a client filtering `attributePlans`, which walks a different set

fields.name: axes
fields.description: (SPARSE) The axes a position is named along -- the ones the matrix identifies itself, never the one the source's ids index. **Name a position along every one of them**: a rank-two matrix has one, a rank-three matrix two, and an `at` that names a different set is refused. **One option per matrix, never per position**: a matrix with 19 059 features has 19 059 of those, and the picker offers the axes while the client picks the positions out of the tables they reference, which it already holds access grants for. Offered when at least one of these axes has a stored layout, which is what makes the read one contiguous slice rather than a scan

fields.name: column
fields.description: The column holding the value. Its `name` is what `colorBys`/`filterBys` take, and its `role`, `unit` and `dtype` are declared on the table

fields.name: control
fields.description: Which control this column admits, derived from its role by the same rule the write path enforces: MEASURE takes a colormap and a `min`/`max` range, CATEGORICAL an explicit colour map and a `values` set

fields.name: graphAttribute
fields.description: (GRAPH, network collections only) A per-node value the collection itself carries: a name its manifest declares -- strahler, degree, depth, component, a writer's own column -- or `radius` when the encoding carries one. Present exactly when `table`, `column` and `sparseDataset` are all null. Pass it back as `colorBys[].attribute` with `kind: GRAPH`; always MEASURE, and the one option kind whose values are per node rather than per object

fields.name: joinPath
fields.description: The `references` hops from the table the source's ids land in to `table`. Empty is the direct case. Pass it back verbatim as `colorBys[].joinPath` to select this option

fields.name: sparseDataset
fields.description: (SPARSE) The matrix one slice of which is read, instead of a table column. Present exactly when `table` and `column` are null -- an option is one or the other, never both

fields.name: table
fields.description: The table the value is read from. With an empty `joinPath` this is a table the source's ids key directly

fields.name: target
fields.description: (network collections only) Which row set this option's values belong to. Null is per-object -- every option every other source offers. NODE/EDGE on a graph attribute or on a column of a table whose axes are node-identified (`NETWORK_COLLECTION_NODES`), where it is derived from the table's own shape -- one node axis is per-node, two are per-edge. Informational on the way back in: the mutation re-derives and stamps it, so a caller never sends it on a COLUMN entry

types.name: ColorMap
types.description: The color space format used to interpret color component values.

enumValues.name: BLACK
enumValues.description: A colormap rendering all values as black.

enumValues.name: BLUE
enumValues.description: A monochromatic colormap from black to pure blue.

enumValues.name: BROWN
enumValues.description: A monochromatic colormap from black to brown.

enumValues.name: COOL
enumValues.description: A colormap of cool tones ranging from cyan to magenta.

enumValues.name: CYAN
enumValues.description: A monochromatic colormap from black to cyan.

enumValues.name: DISTINCT
enumValues.description: Qualitative. The hue scatter with saturation and value tiered by rank as well, so two classes that happen to land on nearby hues still separate -- a palette-free take on glasbey. Reach for it when a mask has many classes.

enumValues.name: GREEN
enumValues.description: A monochromatic colormap from black to pure green.

enumValues.name: GREY
enumValues.description: A grayscale colormap from black to white.

enumValues.name: HUES
enumValues.description: Qualitative. A colour per distinct value, scattered around the hue wheel by the golden ratio so consecutive classes land far apart. The default categorical palette, and the one the id hash itself paints with.

enumValues.name: INFERNO
enumValues.description: The perceptually uniform inferno colormap, ranging from black through red to yellow.

enumValues.name: INTENSITY
enumValues.description: A grayscale colormap mapping intensity values directly to brightness.

enumValues.name: MAGENTA
enumValues.description: A monochromatic colormap from black to magenta.

enumValues.name: MAGMA
enumValues.description: The perceptually uniform magma colormap, ranging from black through purple to light yellow.

enumValues.name: ORANGE
enumValues.description: A monochromatic colormap from black to orange.

enumValues.name: PASTEL
enumValues.description: Qualitative. The hue scatter at low saturation, for a colouring meant to sit under something else rather than carry the picture.

enumValues.name: PINK
enumValues.description: A monochromatic colormap from black to pink.

enumValues.name: PLASMA
enumValues.description: The perceptually uniform plasma colormap, ranging from dark blue to yellow.

enumValues.name: PURPLE
enumValues.description: A monochromatic colormap from black to purple.

enumValues.name: RAINBOW
enumValues.description: A multi-hue rainbow colormap cycling through the visible spectrum.

enumValues.name: RED
enumValues.description: A monochromatic colormap from black to pure red.

enumValues.name: SPECTRAL
enumValues.description: A diverging colormap spanning the spectral colors from red to blue.

enumValues.name: VIRIDIS
enumValues.description: The perceptually uniform viridis colormap, ranging from dark purple to yellow.

enumValues.name: VIVID
enumValues.description: Qualitative. The hue scatter at full saturation, for a colouring meant to carry the picture.

enumValues.name: WARM
enumValues.description: A colormap of warm tones ranging from yellow to red.

enumValues.name: WHITE
enumValues.description: A monochromatic colormap from black to white.

enumValues.name: YELLOW
enumValues.description: A monochromatic colormap from black to yellow.

types.name: ColorSourceKind
types.description: Which sort of source a colouring reads its value from: the discriminator of `LabelColorByInput`, `MeshColorByInput` and `NetworkColorByInput`. Three members, because there are three ways a set of ids reaches a number -- a column of a table they key into, one slice of a sparse matrix they index, or (for a network alone) a per-node value the collection itself carries. Flat with a discriminator rather than an input union, which GraphQL has no such thing as; the fields the other members read are refused rather than ignored. GRAPH is valid only where the source has per-node values to read, which today means a network layer

enumValues.name: COLUMN
enumValues.description: A column of a table the source's ids key into, reached by `table`, `column` and any `joinPath`. Every colouring written before sparse datasets existed is one of these, which is why it is the default.

enumValues.name: GRAPH
enumValues.description: A per-node value the network collection itself carries, reached by `attribute` -- a name its manifest declares (Strahler order, degree, depth, component, a writer's own column), or `radius` when the encoding carries one. Computed once on the full level-0 graph and only ever subset, so the value is the same at every level a node survives to. Always measured, per node rather than per object; `target` says whether it paints nodes or edges.

enumValues.name: SPARSE
enumValues.description: One slice of a sparse matrix the source's ids index, reached by `dataset` and the position `at`. Always measured: a slice is a value per object, so it takes a colormap and never a class map.

types.name: Column
types.description: One declared column of a table dataset: its name, dtype and role. A COORDINATE column is also an axis of the table's space

fields.name: nodeReferences
fields.description: The network collection whose NODE ids this INDEX coordinate column's values are, scoped by the sibling INDEX axis keyed by the same collection's object ids. One such column makes the table per-node, two make it per-edge -- (source, target), in axis declaration order -- which is what a client resolving a per-node picker entry reads the key columns from. Null for every column of every other table

fields.name: references
fields.description: The table whose rows this column's values identify -- a declared foreign key, e.g. an `instance_id` column referencing a table of tracks. The target is keyed by its single INDEX coordinate column; look a value up there. Null for a column that identifies nothing

fields.name: table
fields.description: The table this column is declared on. Trivial when the column was read through its table, load-bearing when it was not -- an options list is flat, and a column with no table on it cannot be named in a `colorBy`

types.name: ColumnColorByInput
types.description: The fields a COLUMN member of a colour picker entry reads. Published for codegen; the wire type is the flat LabelColorByInput / MeshColorByInput / NetworkColorByInput

types.name: ColumnControl
types.description: Which kind of control a column admits, derived from its declared role. The one split that decides how a value becomes a colour and how it is filtered -- published here so a picker renders the control the write path will actually accept.

enumValues.name: CATEGORICAL
enumValues.description: The values name things rather than measuring them, so they take an explicit value-to-colour map and a `values` set. A colormap or a bound over them would impose an order they do not have. Roles ID, TRACK_ID, LABEL and COLOR.

enumValues.name: MEASURE
enumValues.description: The values are measured and ordered, so they take a colormap over their range and a `min`/`max` bound. Roles COORDINATE and ATTRIBUTE.

types.name: ColumnInput
types.description: One column of the table -- THE one declaration a column gets. **Every column of the Parquet is declared, and the declaration is checked against the file** -- same names, same order, same types -- so a declaration that has drifted from the data is refused rather than stored. That check is the whole reason `name` is here: it is a fact about the file, and stating it is how a caller says which file they think they are describing. `dtype` is **optional** -- the server read every column's type off the Parquet when the upload finished, so it is checked when given and taken from the file when not. Given, it is a **DuckDB** type name (`BIGINT`, `DOUBLE`, `VARCHAR`), not a pandas one where a float64 is a `double`. A non-null `axisType` makes the column an axis of the table's own space; **the axis-typed columns, in this list's (= the file's) order, ARE the space** -- a table has no byte order, its axes are named columns, and an edge wanting a different order states its own `inputAxes`/`outputAxes`. `identifiedBy` says what the values are, for an axis and a data column alike

inputFields.name: controls
inputFields.description: Keep only the options admitting these controls: MEASURE for the ones taking a colormap and a range, CATEGORICAL for the ones taking a value set

inputFields.name: directOnly
inputFields.description: Keep only the options whose `joinPath` is empty -- the columns of the tables the collection's ids key directly, with no `references` hop

inputFields.name: roles
inputFields.description: Keep only the options whose column declares one of these roles. Finer than `controls`, which groups the roles into the two the pickers actually branch on

inputFields.name: search
inputFields.description: Case-insensitive substring, matched against the column's name, its `longName` and the name of the table it lives in. The same `icontains` the list queries' `search` uses

inputFields.name: table
inputFields.description: Keep only the options whose value is **read from** this table -- the terminal one, not a table the `joinPath` passes through on the way. An option hopping from A into B is kept by `table: B` and dropped by `table: A`

types.name: ColumnOptionJoinStep
types.description: One hop of a join path: the column whose values identify rows of the next table

fields.name: column
fields.description: The column of it whose `references` identifies rows of the next table

fields.name: table
fields.description: The table this hop stands in

types.name: ColumnRole
types.description: What a table dataset's column is for: a coordinate that places the row, or data hanging off it.

enumValues.name: ATTRIBUTE
enumValues.description: A measurement or property column — area, an intensity, a marker level. Data only; it does not place the row.

enumValues.name: COLOR
enumValues.description: A per-row color, or a value a layer colors the rows by.

enumValues.name: COORDINATE
enumValues.description: A spatial or temporal column whose values are coordinates. The coordinate columns become the axes of the table's own coordinate system, which is what makes the table placeable.

enumValues.name: GROUP_ID
enumValues.description: Groups rows into one connected object — the nodes of one traced arbor, the points of one cluster. Distinct from TRACK_ID, which means a trajectory: a branching tree is not one, and a table that grouped by TRACK_ID would be claiming an order its rows do not have.

enumValues.name: ID
enumValues.description: A per-row identifier.

enumValues.name: LABEL
enumValues.description: A per-row text label.

enumValues.name: TRACK_ID
enumValues.description: Groups rows into a trajectory. Required to render a table as tracks.

types.name: Coordinate
types.description: A discrete coordinate an annotation is pinned to, e.g. a timepoint or a channel

fields.name: name
fields.description: The name of the coordinate, e.g. 't' or 'c'

fields.name: value
fields.description: The value along that coordinate

types.name: CoordinateAnchor
types.description: The axis-agnostic hub that pins metadata spokes (microscope state, OME metadata, value histograms, channel labels, light paths, phasor distributions and calibrations) to specific coordinates of an array, table or sparse dataset. Exactly one of `dataset`, `table` and `sparse` is set

fields.name: coordinates
fields.description: The coordinates this anchor is pinned to, e.g. {'c': 0, 't': 5}. For an array dataset these are level-0 pixel indices, i.e. coordinates of its INTRINSIC system; for a table dataset they are values of its coordinate columns, keyed by column name; for a sparse dataset they are positions along its enumerated axes. An anchor that omits an axis is global along it

fields.name: dataset
fields.description: The array dataset this anchor pins into, or null otherwise

fields.name: microscope
fields.description: The microscope state recorded at this coordinate

fields.name: omeMetadata
fields.description: The OME image metadata recorded at this coordinate

fields.name: sparse
fields.description: The sparse dataset this anchor pins into, or null otherwise

fields.name: table
fields.description: The table dataset this anchor pins into, or null otherwise

inputFields.name: ids
inputFields.description: Filter by list of IDs

types.name: CoordinateAnchorInput
types.description: Input type for a coordinate anchor, which specifies a list of dimension anchors to anchor to

types.name: CoordinateGraph
types.description: The connected component of the coordinate graph around one system: every coordinate system it relates to, and every top-level edge between them. Reachability is undirected -- an edge pointing *into* the system you started from (the edge into a physical space, say) relates to it just as much as one pointing out -- but every edge is returned in its true stored direction, so composing a path is still the client's job and still needs the inversions flagged

fields.name: root
fields.description: The coordinate system the walk started from

fields.name: systems
fields.description: Every coordinate system reachable from the root, the root included, ordered by ID

fields.name: transformations
fields.description: Every top-level edge with both endpoints in `systems`, ordered by ID. The children of a SEQUENCE / BY_DIMENSION wrapper are not listed here; they hang off their wrapper

types.name: CoordinateInput
types.description: A discrete coordinate an annotation is pinned to, e.g. a timepoint or a channel

types.name: CoordinateSystem
types.description: A named coordinate space: a node in the transformation graph. Its axes are ordered, and that order is the order of the array's dimensions

fields.name: annotations
fields.description: The annotations drawn in a space that can reach this one. Reachability, not containment: an annotation belongs to a collection, and outlives every scene composing over this space. A property of the space rather than of any scene over it, which is why it hangs off the system -- ask it of a scene as `worldCoordinateSystem { annotations }`

fields.name: axes
fields.description: The system's axes, in the order the data has them: for a system backed by an array, its store's dimension order; for a table, its coordinate columns as declared. No ordering by type is imposed on either. What matters downstream is that the *spatial* axes are in array order, which is what the render axes are derived from

fields.name: epoch
fields.description: The wall-clock instant this system's time axis has its origin at: `wall_clock = epoch + t * unit`. A property of the space, not of any composition over it. Meaningful only for a unit-carrying system with a TIME axis (a shared world space); null when the clock is unanchored -- the time axis is still a perfectly composable relative coordinate

fields.name: inView
fields.description: Which registered sources are in view of an axis-aligned region asked in *this* system's coordinates, each with its extent here, the path of edges that places it, and its in-view coordinate anchors. The field hangs off the coordinate system because the system IS the frame the region is written in -- there is no ambient world to be wrong about, and no camera: a region is a box, and projecting a frustum into one is the client's job. `region` names a leading prefix of this system's axes and says nothing about the rest, so a 2D box asked of a 4D space constrains only its first two axes. Sources the server cannot bound (a mesh collection's vertices and a table's rows live in Parquet it never opens) come back with an empty `extent` and an `extentState` saying why, rather than being culled -- refusing to bound something is not the same as knowing it is out of view. Nothing is stored: the extent is composed per request from the shapes and the edges, so refining a registration moves everything that looks through it and no cached box can disagree. A source registered per index -- a per-channel or per-timepoint correction -- comes back with `extentState: CONDITIONAL` and no extent unless you pass `at`: it is genuinely in the space, but which box it occupies depends on the coordinate. Individual annotations are out of scope; selecting those needs the region pulled back into their frame, and this server composes forward only

fields.name: placedSystems
fields.description: Every space whose data can be composed here: those reaching this one across steps that compose into one affine map, walking the transformation edges. Composed, not merely connected -- a space reaching this one only across a FIELD relates to it by the values of an array and yields no matrix to draw with, so it is not here. The same set the `placeableIn` filters answer from, so a picker and a layer mutation cannot disagree. Distinct from `coordinateGraph`, which walks the undirected *neighbourhood* -- this is directed, and asks who can get in

fields.name: provenanceEntries
fields.description: Provenance entries for this coordinate system: who created it, and every subsequent change

fields.name: registrations
fields.description: Every top-level edge landing in this space -- the claims that place something here. They belong to the space, so every scene composing over this system sees the same list, each entry unique for its data-tree, and `layers.pathToWorld` searches exactly these plus the datasets' own facts. On a shared world these are the registrations a client authored; on a container's own grid they are the lens crops and derived children that land in it. Composing the matrices stays the client's job. Not filtered by kind, so a table's own system also lists the FIELD edge of any mask keying it -- that one places nothing (a FIELD has no inverse, so no path walks it backwards); it is a dereference, and `attributePlans` is what reads it

fields.name: residents
fields.description: The data living in this space. Empty for a pure reference frame -- a world, an atlas -- which is what a space with no residents *is*; there is no separate kind to consult. Several residents may share one space: a dataset's own pyramid levels and unsliced lenses live in its grid, and a hundred tiles acquired on one stage can be registered into one stage frame

fields.name: scenes
fields.description: The scenes that compose over this system as their world. A SHARED space lists every scene sharing it and outlives each of them: a scene adopts a space, never owns it, and deleting a scene never deletes the space. The inverse of `Scene.worldCoordinateSystem`

fields.name: transformVersion
fields.description: How many times the transformation chain from this system down to its dataset's intrinsic pixel space has been written, as it stands now. Compare it with an annotation's `createdWithTransforms` to detect staleness: the two agreeing means the geometry was authored against the chain still in force, and them differing means an edge on the path has been written since. Only the comparison is meaningful -- the number counts history rows, so it also moves when an edge is merely renamed, which errs towards recomputing a box that did not need it rather than trusting one that did. 0 for a system that IS an intrinsic space, or one with no path down to pixels (a unit-carrying or shared space -- its coordinates are meaningful on their own). Provenance only: it never takes part in resolving a coordinate

fields.name: visualizations
fields.description: Everything laid out over this system as its world, of every kind: its scenes, then its charts. The inverse of `Visualization.worldCoordinateSystem`. Unpaginated -- for a filtered or paged list of one kind, ask `scenes` here or the top-level `charts`

types.name: CoordinateSystemDerivedFromInput

types.name: CreatableTransformKind
types.description: The kind of a transformation a client can author directly: the discriminator of `TransformInput`. SEQUENCE is absent on purpose -- it is a wrapper the ingest builds together with its children (pyramid levels, stepped lenses), never authored empty.

enumValues.name: AFFINE
enumValues.description: A general affine map. Takes `affine`, an M x (N+1) matrix with rows outermost.

enumValues.name: BY_DIMENSION
enumValues.description: A map acting on a named subset of the axes and saying nothing about the rest. Takes `inputAxes` and `outputAxes`, and optionally `scale`, `translation` or `affine` acting on the named axes.

enumValues.name: FIELD
enumValues.description: A non-affine map given by the values of an array rather than by a formula. Takes `field` (the array's coordinate system), `inputAxes` and `outputAxes`.

enumValues.name: IDENTITY
enumValues.description: The identity map. Input and output coordinates are the same, so it takes no parameters.

enumValues.name: MAP_AXIS
enumValues.description: A permutation of axes, mapping each input axis to an output axis by name. Takes `inputAxes` and `outputAxes`; the matrix is synthesized from them.

enumValues.name: ROTATION
enumValues.description: A rotation. Takes `affine`: the orthonormal matrix, in the same layout an AFFINE uses.

enumValues.name: SCALE
enumValues.description: A per-axis multiplication. Takes `scale`, one entry per input axis.

enumValues.name: TRANSLATION
enumValues.description: A per-axis offset. Takes `translation`, one entry per input axis.

enumValues.name: UNMAPPABLE
enumValues.description: A declared NON-correspondence: no point of either space maps to a point of the other. Takes only an optional `reason`.

Exactly one of `dataset`, `table` and `sparse` names the container; `anchor` carries the coordinates and the spokes. types.description: Create a SHARED coordinate system -- a reference space with no owner, e.g. a world or an atlas -- and, in the same call, author the edges registering any number of sources (datasets, table datasets, mesh collections, coordinate systems) into it. Every other system is owned by a container and created with it, so a shared space is the only system created directly. createSceneFromCoordinateSystem later builds a scene over it and materializes those sources as layers

types.name: CreateSceneFromCoordinateSystemInput
types.description: Bootstrap a renderable scene over an existing coordinate system. Over an ownerless SHARED space the sources already registered into it become layers, up to the policy's nchildren sources -- each source's path to world is the one registration createCoordinateSystem authored. Over an owned system (a dataset's intrinsic pixels, a physical space, a collection's space) the container's own data becomes the layer: it is in its own space by construction, so no edge exists or is authored. A multi-channel image becomes one layer per channel, each with its own hue, order and visibility, so a viewer can control the channels separately; an RGB photograph stays one layer. Rerunning makes another scene over the same space, which outlives them all

inputFields.name: policy
inputFields.defaultValue: {includeMeshes: true, includeNetworks: true, kind: null, nchildren: 8, skipUnplaceable: false, transformTables: false}

types.name: CreateSceneFromLensInput
types.description: Bootstrap a renderable scene showing one lens: its selection and nothing else of its dataset, one layer per channel exactly as createSceneFromCoordinateSystem draws a whole dataset. This is how a crop is staged -- staging a sliced lens' *space* draws its whole dataset again, because which lens the layers read is not a fact of the space

types.name: CreateSeriesChartLayerInput

The coordinate column is not named here -- it is whichever of the table's coordinate columns its registration maps onto the chart's axis. The table must already be registered into the chart's world: this writes no edge

types.name: CreateSparseDatasetInput
types.description: Create a sparse dataset from one uploaded sparse store, which holds the matrix in one or more layouts. A sparse matrix is a grid of numbers with no row labels and no column labels, so **every axis says what its positions are** through its own `identifiedBy` -- a source whose contents are the ids, or the table whose rows they are. Carried on the axis, identified-exactly-once is a property of this input rather than a rule the server enforces. Nothing about the matrix itself is declared: the spec, shape, each layout's encoding and its chunking were read from the store when its upload was finished, and are checked against these axes rather than taken from them

enumValues.description: An array dataset as a whole, through its intrinsic pixel grid. Use it when the source is the entire image and there is no lens worth minting.

enumValues.name: LENS
enumValues.description: A selection over an array dataset, and the preferred way to name one: a lens' own edge back to its dataset already carries the crop, so pointing at it gets the rest of the chain for free.

enumValues.name: MESH_COLLECTION
enumValues.description: A mesh collection, through its vertex coordinate system.

enumValues.name: TABLE_DATASET
enumValues.description: A table dataset, through the space its coordinate columns declare -- the direction an image reconstructed from a table of SMLM localizations is derived. A table with no coordinate columns enumerates objects rather than places them, and its only honest edge is UNMAPPABLE.

types.name: DerivedFromInput
types.description: Where this data came from, as a discriminated union: `kind` selects which sort of source is being named, and only that member's id field is read -- any other is rejected. The member inputs annotated `@unionElementOf(union: "DerivedFromInput")` say which field each kind reads. Direction is always this data -> its source

inputFields.name: annotationCollection
inputFields.description: (ANNOTATION_COLLECTION) The annotation collection this data was computed from

inputFields.name: coordinateSystem
inputFields.description: (COORDINATE_SYSTEM) The space this data was computed from, when the source is a space rather than a container

inputFields.name: dataset
inputFields.description: (DATASET) The array dataset this data was computed from, through its whole pixel grid

inputFields.name: kind
inputFields.description: Which sort of thing the source is. It fixes which id field below is read; any other is rejected

inputFields.name: lens
inputFields.description: (LENS) The lens this data was computed from

inputFields.name: meshCollection
inputFields.description: (MESH_COLLECTION) The mesh collection this data was computed from

inputFields.name: tableDataset
inputFields.description: (TABLE_DATASET) The table this data was computed from -- an SMLM localization table a reconstruction was rendered from, say

inputFields.name: transform
inputFields.description: How this data's own space maps back into the source's -- any creatable kind; the rank check holds you to it. **Omit it and the edge is UNMAPPABLE**: naming a source records the lineage and claims no geometry, which is the truth for a table of per-object measurements whose rows are not anywhere. State IDENTITY for an in-place operation, TRANSLATION for a crop, SCALE for a resample or for a localization table's nanometres into a reconstruction's pixels, BY_DIMENSION for a projection that drops an axis. Only a mappable edge carries placement: derived data sits where its source sits exactly when it says how

inputFields.name: valueRelation
inputFields.description: What the derivation did to the *values* -- orthogonal to the transform's `kind`, which only says where the data sits: IDENTICAL for a crop or reorder (statistics transfer), TRANSFORMED for a deconvolution, a normalization, or a table of measurements read off an image, CATEGORIZED for a threshold or segmentation (values became labels -- a bootstrapped scene then renders as a label map). Omit when unstated; the algorithm itself belongs to task provenance

types.name: DesociateInput
types.description: An input for releasing a set of items from another item, e.g. removing images from a dataset

inputFields.name: other
inputFields.description: The ID of the target item

inputFields.name: selfs
inputFields.description: The IDs of the items to release

types.description: Detector

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Element kind

fields.name: label
fields.description: Element label

fields.name: ports
fields.description: List of ports on the element

fields.name: pose
fields.description: 3D pose of the element

types.name: DetectorElementInput
types.description: The fields a DETECTOR element reads. Published for codegen; the wire type is the flat OpticalElementInput

types.name: DeviceState
types.description: One hardware device's recorded state

fields.name: kind
fields.description: A free-form device kind, e.g. 'laser', 'filter-wheel'

fields.name: label
fields.description: The device's identity in the setup, e.g. 'filter-wheel-1'

types.name: DeviceStateInput
types.description: One hardware device's recorded state: its identity in the setup plus its settings at this coordinate

inputFields.name: kind
inputFields.description: A free-form device kind, e.g. 'laser', 'filter-wheel'

inputFields.name: label
inputFields.description: The device's identity in the setup, e.g. 'filter-wheel-1'

types.name: Easing
types.description: How a viewer eases the camera along the travel into an animation waypoint.

enumValues.name: EASE_IN
enumValues.description: Start slow, arrive at full speed. Right for the first leg, pulling away from rest.

enumValues.name: EASE_IN_OUT
enumValues.description: Slow at both ends, quick in the middle. The default: it reads as deliberate on a leg that stands alone.

enumValues.name: EASE_OUT
enumValues.description: Start at full speed, arrive slowly. Right for the last leg, settling onto the final pose.

enumValues.name: LINEAR
enumValues.description: Constant speed the whole way. Right for a leg in the middle of a continuous move, where an ease would read as a stutter.

types.name: Embedding
types.description: A stored vector, as `<model id>:<comma-separated floats>` -- e.g. `potion-base-8M:0.0123,-0.0456,...`. The model id is part of the value because vectors from different models are not comparable. Null when the row has no vector (it carries no text, or the model was unavailable when it was saved).

types.name: Euler
types.description: Euler angles for 3D orientation

types.name: EulerInput
types.description: Euler angles representing rotation in 3D space.

types.name: ExportOfInput
types.description: The container this file was written from, as a discriminated union: `kind` selects which sort of container is being named, and only that member's id field is read -- any other is rejected. The member inputs annotated `@unionElementOf(union: "ExportOfInput")` say which field each kind reads. Direction is always this file -> the data it was written from

inputFields.name: annotationCollection
inputFields.description: (ANNOTATION_COLLECTION) The annotation collection this file was written from

inputFields.name: dataset
inputFields.description: (DATASET) The array dataset this file was written from

inputFields.name: kind
inputFields.description: Which sort of thing the container is. It fixes which id field below is read; any other is rejected

inputFields.name: meshCollection
inputFields.description: (MESH_COLLECTION) The mesh collection this file was written from

inputFields.name: seriesIdentifier
inputFields.description: Which part of the file this concerns -- the series of a multi-series LIF or CZI, the sheet of a workbook. Omit when the file holds one thing. It is part of the link's identity, not a label on it: one dataset fused from two series of one file is two links, and two links naming the same file and the same series are refused

inputFields.name: tableDataset
inputFields.description: (TABLE_DATASET) The table dataset this file was written from

inputFields.name: valueRelation
inputFields.description: What the conversion did to the *values*: IDENTICAL for a lossless transcode (a CZI to a Zarr, a dataset to an OME-TIFF), TRANSFORMED for a projection or a contrast-stretched PNG, CATEGORIZED when the values became labels. Omit when unstated; the converter and its parameters belong to task provenance

types.name: ExtentState
types.description: Whether the server can state where a source sits in a space, and if not, why not. Derived, never stored.

enumValues.name: CONDITIONAL
enumValues.description: The source reaches this space only across a selector-scoped edge — a per-channel or per-timepoint correction — so where it sits depends on a coordinate this query did not fix. The source is returned, because it genuinely is in the space; `extent` is empty because there is no single box, not because none could be computed. Ask again with `at` to get one.

enumValues.name: INVERTED
enumValues.description: The path walks an edge against its stored direction, and the extent walk composes forward only -- it pushes a box, and re-bounding one through an inverted step is a different calculation. The step *is* invertible: a placement search offers a backwards step only for a map that has an inverse, which is why `Layer.asAffine` composes such a path without difficulty. So compose `path` yourself, inverting the flagged step, or read the layer's `asAffine`.

enumValues.name: KNOWN
enumValues.description: The extent is stated, over the axes it names and only those.

enumValues.name: NON_AFFINE
enumValues.description: A FIELD edge on the path gives the map as the values of an array rather than as a formula, so there is no closed form to push a box through. The path is real and is returned; `invariance` reads DIFFEOMORPHIC.

enumValues.name: UNREADABLE
enumValues.description: The source's geometry is not something the server holds: a mesh collection's vertices and a table dataset's rows live in Parquet it never opens. `extent` is null because there is no box to push, not because the path failed -- and the source is returned anyway, because refusing to bound something is not the same as knowing it is out of view.

types.name: FabriksAccessGrant
types.description: Temporary S3 credentials for reading a fabriks store. Covers the whole prefix, so one grant reads the manifest, both catalogs and every level.

types.name: FabriksLike
types.description: A reference to an uploaded **fabriks store**: one prefix holding `fabriks.json`, both catalogs and every octree level. Request it with `requestFabriksUpload`, write the tree, land the manifest last, then `finishFabriksUpload` -- which reads the manifest and refuses a prefix without one. A collection registered this way declares no grid and no encoding: the server reads them from the artifact, so they cannot be stated wrong

types.name: FabriksStore
types.description: A fabriks collection stored as a prefix of Parquet files behind the S3 datalayer. Its grid and encoding are read from its own manifest, never declared by a caller.

fields.name: accessGrant
fields.description: Get temporary S3 read credentials covering this store's whole prefix -- the manifest, both catalogs and every level, in one grant.

fields.name: maxBytes
fields.description: The byte budget the upload grant advertised for this store. Advertised, not enforced: a session policy bounds what a credential may write, never how much, so a store may exceed this

fields.name: sizeBytes
fields.description: How many bytes this store actually holds, measured when its upload was finished. Null while unfinished, or for stores written before this was recorded

types.name: FabriksUploadGrant
types.description: Temporary S3 credentials for uploading a fabriks store. Scoped to the prefix and permitted to read back and delete inside it, because the tree is written incrementally and its manifest lands last.

types.name: FieldTransformInput
types.description: The fields a FIELD member of TransformInput reads. Published for codegen; the wire type is the flat TransformInput

types.name: FieldTransformation
types.description: A non-affine map given by the values of an array rather than by a formula. The array is a `field`: a node of this graph, not a payload on this edge, so it keeps its own lineage and its axes say what its numbers mean. It has no closed-form inverse, so a placement path never walks it backwards

fields.name: field
fields.description: The coordinate system of the array whose values are this map. Its value axis says what they mean: COORDINATE for absolute positions, DISPLACEMENT for offsets, none at all for a scalar array whose single value is a position. Equal to `input` when the array's own pixels are the map, as for a label mask keying a table of objects

fields.name: input
fields.description: The system this edge maps from. Null for the child of a SEQUENCE or BY_DIMENSION, which takes its endpoints from the wrapper

fields.name: inputAxes
fields.description: The names of the input axes this edge's parameters are ordered by. `scale`, `translation` and the columns of `affine` follow this order -- which is the input system's axis order, NOT the reading layer's axis names, and the two differ often enough that indexing the arrays against them silently misplaces them. A BY_DIMENSION edge names only the subset of axes it acts on; the axes it does not name are the ones it leaves untouched

fields.name: invariance
fields.description: Which geometric properties survive this edge's map, derived from `kind`: ISOMETRY (distances, angles and areas all transfer), SIMILARITY (angles and length ratios transfer, absolute lengths scale by one common factor), AFFINE (parallelism and area ratios transfer, angles and distances do not), DIFFEOMORPHIC (topology at best, and only locally -- the Jacobian varies with position), NONE (nothing corresponds). A SEQUENCE or BY_DIMENSION is the weakest of its children. Stated by kind, never by inspecting the numbers: an AFFINE edge reads AFFINE even when its matrix happens to be rigid, because separating those needs an SVD. A layer's `placementInvariance` is the minimum of this over its whole path to world

fields.name: output
fields.description: The system this edge maps to. Null for the child of a SEQUENCE or BY_DIMENSION, which takes its endpoints from the wrapper

fields.name: outputAxes
fields.description: The names of the output axes this edge produces. For a rank-changing BY_DIMENSION edge (placing a (c,y,x) dataset into a (t,z,y,x) world) this is the subset it maps onto; the world's other axes are untouched

fields.name: provenanceEntries
fields.description: Provenance entries for this edge: who authored it, and every refinement since. A refinement rewrites the edge in place, so this audit trail is where the placement's earlier states live -- and counting these rows along a chain is what `CoordinateSystem.transformVersion` reports

fields.name: selector
fields.description: Where along one axis this edge applies, or null for an edge that holds everywhere -- which is almost every edge. A per-channel correction is scoped to {axis: "c", index: 2}; several such edges over one axis are one piecewise map. A path query crosses a scoped edge only when it fixes that coordinate with `at`

fields.name: validity
fields.description: How much this map is actually known: VALIDATED for a map the server derived (or one someone checked), INFERRED for numbers read from metadata, MANUAL for an authored registration, UNKNOWN for one its author marked as a guess. A layer's validity is the weakest edge on its path to world

fields.name: valueRelation
fields.description: (derivation edges) What the operation this edge records did to the *values*, orthogonal to `kind`: IDENTICAL (a crop -- statistics transfer), TRANSFORMED (a deconvolution -- same quantity, new numbers), CATEGORIZED (a threshold -- values became labels, and a bootstrapped scene renders the data as a label map). Null when unstated, and never present on a registration -- values do not cross a claim between spaces

fields.name: version
fields.description: How many times this edge has been written, counting the row that created it -- so a new edge reads 1. Only comparison is meaningful: this and the edge's `id` together are the cache key for anything derived from the edge, and a change means refetch. It counts the same provenance rows `provenanceEntries` lists, so the audit trail and the token cannot disagree; a rename moves it too, which errs towards refetching something that did not change rather than trusting something that did

types.name: File
types.description: A file in its original format (e.g. a microscopy vendor file), stored in a BigFileStore. Files are the raw bytes that array datasets, table datasets and mesh collections are converted from.

fields.name: contentType
fields.description: The content type of the file

fields.name: createdThrough
fields.description: The task this file was created through, if any

fields.name: createdThroughBy
fields.description: The assigner of the creating task, if any

fields.name: creator
fields.description: The user who created this file

fields.name: derivedContainers
fields.description: The containers converted out of this file: the datasets a converter wrote from it, one per series. **Not a derivation** -- a file has no coordinate system, so these links claim no geometry and place nothing; they say only that this file's bytes and that data are the same thing

fields.name: descriptors
fields.description: This object's descriptors, a flat mapping of key to value: the facts about it that an action's port can `require` and a trigger can test (e.g. `@mikro/n_channels`). The keys are the ones mikro declares for this structure, and the values are the ones a signal about the object carries. Empty for a structure that declares none

fields.name: exportedFrom
fields.description: The containers this file was written from: the dataset exported to OME-TIFF, the mesh collection written to STL. The mirror of `derivedContainers`

fields.name: folder
fields.description: The folder this file is filed in, or null once its folder was deleted (deleting a folder unfiles what is in it and destroys nothing). Organisational only: it says where a user keeps the file, nothing about its contents

fields.name: organization
fields.description: The organization this file belongs to

fields.name: provenanceEntries
fields.description: Provenance entries for this file

fields.name: size
fields.description: The size of the file in bytes

inputFields.name: assignedBy
inputFields.description: Filter by the sub of the user that assigned the creating task

inputFields.name: createdAfter
inputFields.description: Filter for items created after this datetime

inputFields.name: createdBefore
inputFields.description: Filter for items created before this datetime

inputFields.name: createdThrough
inputFields.description: Filter by the database ID of the task the item was created through (the `createdThrough { id }` field)

inputFields.name: createdThroughBy
inputFields.description: Filter by the database ID of the user that assigned the creating task (the `createdThroughBy { id }` field)

inputFields.name: createdThroughTask
inputFields.description: Filter by the rekuest task id the item was created through

inputFields.name: exportedFrom
inputFields.description: Filter to the files written out of this container -- the OME-TIFF a dataset was exported to. The opposite direction from `sourceOf`

inputFields.name: extension
inputFields.description: Filter by file extension, case-insensitively and with the leading dot optional: `czi`, `.czi` and `CZI` are the same request, and `ome.tiff` matches only the double extension. A normalizing convenience over `name: {iEndsWith: ".czi"}`, which is still there if you want the raw lookup

inputFields.name: folder
inputFields.description: Filter by the folder this file belongs to

inputFields.name: folders
inputFields.description: Filter by a list of folder IDs

inputFields.name: hasMetadata
inputFields.description: Filter by whether any unstructured metadata has been attached to the file

inputFields.name: hasStore
inputFields.description: Filter by whether the file's bytes ever arrived: false finds the `File` rows whose upload was granted and never completed, which carry no store at all

inputFields.name: ids
inputFields.description: Filter by list of IDs

inputFields.name: linkedTo
inputFields.description: Filter to the files linked to this container in *either* direction: read into it or written out of it. Use `sourceOf` or `exportedFrom` when the direction matters

inputFields.name: mimeGroup
inputFields.description: Filter to the files holding one sort of thing. Derived from the extension at query time and stored nowhere -- see `FileMimeGroup`, which explains why this reads the name rather than `contentType`. A curated list, so treat it as a picker convenience and filter on `name` or `contentType` when you need an exact answer

inputFields.name: notDerived
inputFields.description: Filter for files nothing was exported into: the raw sources a converter read, as opposed to the files written out of data already here. Reads the file's links, which replaced the `origins` M2M -- that column was never written by any resolver, so this filter used to answer `true` for every file in the database

inputFields.name: owner
inputFields.description: Filter by the creator's subject ID

inputFields.name: populated
inputFields.description: Filter by whether the upload completed. **Implies a store**: a file with no store at all is `hasStore: false`, not `populated: false`, so the two are not complementary and combining `hasStore: false` with `populated: false` matches nothing

inputFields.name: search
inputFields.description: Search by name (case-insensitive substring)

inputFields.name: seriesIdentifier
inputFields.description: Filter to files linked under this series of a multi-series file -- 'series-3' of a LIF. Matches on any link, in either direction

inputFields.name: sourceOf
inputFields.description: Filter to the files this container was produced from -- the CZI a converter read to write its arrays. The file-side mirror of `ArrayDatasetFilter.sourceFile`, and the reason this takes a `{kind, id}` rather than a bare ID: dataset 3 and table 3 both exist, so an unqualified id could not say which was meant

inputFields.name: unlinked
inputFields.description: Filter for files no data references at all -- the uploads nothing was ever converted from and nothing was ever written into. The orphans, in other words: what a cleanup view wants. `notDerived` is the weaker question (nothing was *exported* into it), so every unlinked file is also notDerived, and not the reverse

types.name: FileLike
types.description: The `FileLike` scalar type represents a reference to a big file storage previously created by the user n a datalayer

types.name: FileLink
types.description: A file and a container holding the same data, and which of the two was made from the other. **Not a derivation**: `derivedFrom` states how one space maps into another, and a file has no space, so this claims no geometry and no placement -- only that these bytes and this data are the same thing

fields.name: container
fields.description: The data side of the link. Exactly one container is set on a link, and this is it

fields.name: createdThrough
fields.description: The task this link was created through, if any

fields.name: createdThroughBy
fields.description: The assigner of the creating task, if any

fields.name: creator
fields.description: The user who recorded this link

fields.name: direction
fields.description: Which side was made from the other: SOURCE when the container was produced from the file (an ingest), RENDITION when the file was written from the container (an export)

fields.name: file
fields.description: The file side of the link

fields.name: organization
fields.description: The organization this link belongs to

fields.name: provenanceEntries
fields.description: Provenance entries for this link

fields.name: seriesIdentifier
fields.description: Which part of the file this link concerns -- the series of a multi-series LIF or CZI. Empty when the file holds one thing. Part of the link's identity, so a dataset fused from two series of one file has two links

fields.name: valueRelation
fields.description: What the conversion did to the values: IDENTICAL for a lossless transcode, TRANSFORMED for a projection or a contrast-stretched export. Null when unstated

types.name: FileLinkContainer
types.description: The data side of a file link: a container whose contents a file encodes

types.name: FileLinkContainerKind
types.description: Which sort of container a file link names: the discriminator of `ExportOfInput`. Only the four containers that hold data a file can be written from or read into -- a lens is a selection over a dataset rather than a thing with its own bytes, and a coordinate system is a space, which no file encodes

enumValues.name: ANNOTATION_COLLECTION
enumValues.description: An annotation collection, the container a GeoJSON or ROI file is loaded into.

enumValues.name: DATASET
enumValues.description: An array dataset -- the container an image file is converted into, and the one an OME-TIFF is written from.

enumValues.name: MESH_COLLECTION
enumValues.description: A mesh collection, the container an STL or OBJ file is loaded into.

enumValues.name: TABLE_DATASET
enumValues.description: A table dataset, the container a CSV or parquet file is loaded into.

types.name: FileLinkContainerRef
types.description: One container a file link points at: `kind` says which sort of thing it is, `id` says which one. Structured rather than a bare ID because a link can name four different kinds of container and their ids are drawn from separate sequences -- dataset 3 and table dataset 3 both exist, and an unqualified 3 could not choose

inputFields.name: id
inputFields.description: The container's ID, in the sequence its `kind` names

inputFields.name: kind
inputFields.description: Which sort of container. It fixes which column the filter reads

types.name: FileLinkDirection
types.description: Which side of a file link was made from the other. A file is a store, not a container -- it has no coordinate system -- so this relates bytes to data rather than two spaces, and it is deliberately not a `DerivedFromInput` kind. Direction has to be stated because nothing else records which side existed first

enumValues.name: RENDITION
enumValues.description: The file was produced from the container: a dataset written out as OME-TIFF, a mesh exported to STL. This is the export direction, and the container existed first.

enumValues.name: SOURCE
enumValues.description: The container was produced from the file: a CZI a converter read to write a Zarr dataset, a CSV a table was loaded from. This is the ingest direction, and the file existed first.

inputFields.name: assignedBy
inputFields.description: Filter by the sub of the user that assigned the creating task

inputFields.name: createdAfter
inputFields.description: Filter for items created after this datetime

inputFields.name: createdBefore

inputFields.description: Filter by the database ID of the user that assigned the creating task (the `createdThroughBy { id }` field)

inputFields.name: owner

types.name: FileMimeGroup
types.description: A coarse bucket for what sort of thing a file holds, for a picker that wants "just the images". **Derived at query time from the file's extension, never stored** -- so it cannot drift from the file it describes, and it is a filter only. Classified by extension rather than by `contentType` on purpose: a CZI, LIF or ND2 is uploaded as `application/octet-stream`, so a content-type rule would file every vendor image under OTHER, which is precisely the case worth finding. `contentType` is the fallback when the extension is unknown. It is a curated list, not an authority: filter on `name` or `contentType` directly when you need an exact answer

enumValues.name: ANNOTATION
enumValues.description: Shapes and regions: geojson, roi, zip-of-rois, xml.

enumValues.name: ARCHIVE
enumValues.description: Containers of other files: zip, tar, gz, 7z. A zipped acquisition is an ARCHIVE, not an IMAGE -- the extension is all this reads.

enumValues.name: DOCUMENT
enumValues.description: Human-readable notes and reports: pdf, txt, md, docx.

enumValues.name: IMAGE
enumValues.description: Bioimage and picture formats: the vendor files (czi, lif, nd2, oib, lsm, ims, scn, svs) plus tiff/ome.tiff, png and jpeg.

enumValues.name: MESH
enumValues.description: Surface geometry: stl, obj, ply, off.

enumValues.name: OTHER
enumValues.description: Nothing the curated list recognizes, and no usable `contentType`. Includes every file with no extension at all.

enumValues.name: TABLE
enumValues.description: Tabular data: csv, tsv, parquet, feather, xlsx.

types.name: FilterByOption
types.description: One column a layer may be filtered by, and how it is reached. The same set the colour-options query returns, under the name that reads right where a rule is being authored: both pickers turn on the same measure-vs-categorical split, so the candidates are one answer and this is the second way to ask for it. Every option returned is one the mutation that publishes the picker accepts -- `createMeshLayer(filterBys:)` over a collection, `createLabelLayer(render: {filterBys: ...})` over a lens

fields.name: axes
fields.description: (SPARSE) The axes a position is named along -- the ones the matrix identifies itself, never the one the source's ids index. **Name a position along every one of them**: a rank-two matrix has one, a rank-three matrix two, and an `at` that names a different set is refused. **One option per matrix, never per position**: a matrix with 19 059 features has 19 059 of those, and the picker offers the axes while the client picks the positions out of the tables they reference, which it already holds access grants for. Offered when at least one of these axes has a stored layout, which is what makes the read one contiguous slice rather than a scan

fields.name: column
fields.description: The column the rule is written against. Its `name` is what `filterBys` takes, and its `unit` is the unit a `min`/`max` bound is stated in

fields.name: control
fields.description: Which rule this column admits, derived from its role by the same rule the write path enforces: MEASURE takes a `min`/`max` bound, CATEGORICAL an explicit `values` set. Passing the wrong one is refused at the boundary

fields.name: graphAttribute
fields.description: (GRAPH, network collections only) A per-node value the collection itself carries, exactly as on `ColorByOption`. Present exactly when `table`, `column` and `sparseDataset` are all null. Pass it back as `filterBys[].attribute` with `kind: GRAPH`; always MEASURE, so the rule is `min`/`max` bounds, and it hides individual nodes and segments rather than whole objects

fields.name: joinPath
fields.description: The `references` hops from the table the ids land in to `table`. Empty is the direct case. Pass it back verbatim as `filterBys[].joinPath` to write a rule against this column

fields.name: sparseDataset
fields.description: (SPARSE) The matrix one slice of which is read, instead of a table column. Present exactly when `table` and `column` are null -- an option is one or the other, never both

fields.name: table
fields.description: The table the value is read from. With an empty `joinPath` this is a table the source's ids key directly

fields.name: target
fields.description: (network collections only) Which row set a rule over this option hides, exactly as on `ColorByOption`: null keeps or drops whole objects, NODE hides nodes and their segments, EDGE hides segments alone. Derived from the table's shape and stamped by the mutation, never sent on a COLUMN rule

types.name: FilterElement
types.description: A filter

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Element kind
